conviction_note: Near-non-result. JPX pre-released its H1 on 2026-09-24 (FY NI 98.5bn to 105bn, DPS 77 to 82), when it already knew almost all of the half. October trading is running below the H2 volume that revised plan implies, and the 20-business-day buyback window closed in July, so the print is unlikely to add a third material raise or a new return. Against that, the street (IFIS FY pretax 164.2bn) already sits about 5% above the plan, the stock is -5.4% over 20 days, and in 2024 and 2025 JPX made a small true-up raise at the H1 print. Findings sum -0.2; scaled -0.15 = (2*0.47-1)*2.5. The two agree in sign and size because the evidence is thin both ways.

findings.finding: The 2026-09-24 forecast assumes 株券等 daily value of ¥11.0tn for the full year. H1 actual was about ¥11.9tn (Q1 12.39tn from the company's Q1 overview; Jul 12.52, Aug 11.29, Sep 10.28 from JPX monthly releases), so the plan implies about ¥10.1tn for H2. October prime regular-session value has averaged about ¥7.7tn over 17 sessions, about ¥9.6tn 株券等-equivalent at the Q1/Sept ratio of 1.24-1.25, roughly 5% below that H2 assumption. The 9/24 revision document carries a 2026-09-18 TDnet id, so it was prepared with nearly all of H1 known. A third material upward revision at this print is therefore unlikely; a hold or a small true-up is the base case, and that stays below the IFIS consensus of 164.2bn pretax.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At the H1 print of 2025-10-29 a +0.8% true-up of an earlier September raise came with -4.93% on the day (-2.72% open to next close), after a 5-day run to highs. At the H1 print of 2024-10-29 a true-up came with +1.91% on the day. Q1 2026-07-28, with a +27% raise and a DPS hike: -2.08% on the day, +1.33% open to next close. The 2026-09-24 pre-release itself: +1.72% on the day, +4.36% open to next close (Yahoo chart, true dates).
findings.why_not_priced: IFIS consensus has sat at 164.2bn pretax, unchanged for four weeks and 4.9% above the plan, so the sell side still marks the plan as conservative and has not reflected October's softer volumes. If it had, consensus would have converged down toward 156.5bn. Partly priced: the daily trading value is public and the stock is -5.4% over 20 days while the Nikkei is near highs.
findings.independence: Daily prime trading value from https://stock-marketdata.com/trading-value.html (October sessions 6.6-10.1tn) and JPX monthly releases https://www.jpx.co.jp/corporate/news/news-releases/0063/20261001-11.html and 20260901-11 / 20260803-11. These are a different source from the company's revision document, but all of it is JPX's own published data.

findings.finding: Q2 (Jul-Sep) 株券等 daily value was ¥11.42tn against ¥12.39tn in Q1 (-7.8%), and TOPIX and Nikkei futures volumes fell in July and August, so Q2 profit steps down from Q1's record 44.06bn pretax. The IFIS cumulative-H1 path (87.2bn) implies an almost flat Q2 at about 43.1bn, which looks stale. Yahoo's one-analyst Q2 EPS of 26.97 already allows for the dip.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: H1 progress rates of 50.9% (2023), 52.9% (2024) and 53.1% (2025) against the plan of the day. This year about 54% on my estimate, which is in line. The quarter itself has not been the mover; the forecast has.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The monthly series is public, the company pre-released the half on 9/24, and the only bar that would show a miss is a possibly stale IFIS quarterly path. Kept small for that reason.
findings.independence: July and August monthly releases (https://www.jpx.co.jp/corporate/news/news-releases/0063/t13vrt000001r9c8-att/topics.pdf, https://www.jpx.co.jp/corporate/news/news-releases/0063/t13vrt000001v97p-att/topics.pdf); Q1 overview https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260728/140120260727500264.pdf. This is the same series as finding 1 but a different line (the reported quarter, not the H2 guide).

findings.finding: The ¥20bn / 40m-share buyback authorised on 2026-04-28 (window 2026-06-01 to 2026-10-26) was completed on 2026-07-07. JPX's last H1 print (2025-10-29) brought a treasury-share cancellation rather than a new buyback, and its buybacks have come at FY prints (Apr 2025, Apr 2026). The interim DPS was already raised to 41 on 9/24 under a payout target of 60% or more. No return catalyst is expected, so a new buyback would be a pure upside surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-04-28 FY print with a ¥20bn buyback: +5.94% on the day, then -4.53% the next day. 2025-10-29 H1 print with a cancellation only: -4.93% on the day.
findings.why_not_priced: Optionality, not information. Nobody expects a buyback at an H1 print here, so if one comes it is unpriced. Expected value is roughly a 10-15% chance times about +3%.
findings.independence: Completion notice of 2026-07-07 (https://kabutan.jp/disclosures/pdf/20260707/140120260707589202/); cancellation-only notice of 2025-10-29 (https://kabutan.jp/disclosures/pdf/20251029/140120251028580284/).

baseline_tension: Mild agreement with the -5.4% 20-day run-up, which already reflects softer volumes. Against the near-zero priced lean (+0.27), the evidence is roughly neutral. The strongest positive the release could carry is a third true-up raise (it happened at the H1 print in 2024 and 2025) or an off-pattern buyback. I looked for both: the buyback finished in July, and October volumes argue against a material raise. So the lean is only slightly negative.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a public series): finding 2 (Q2 down quarter on quarter, from JPX's public monthly volumes) cut from -0.3 to -0.1. Finding 1 cut from -0.5 to -0.4 only, because it rests on what the release ADDS (the forecast decision against the street), not only on the visible series.
